title: Regular constant scalars act monomorphically on flat module sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A$ a commutative ring, and $A_{\mathcal C}$ the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $M$ be a sheaf of $A_{\mathcal C}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] that is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Fix $a\in A$ such that the function $A\to A$, $x\mapsto ax$, is injective. Then multiplication by the constant scalar $a$ is a monomorphism on both $A_{\mathcal C}$ and $M$. Explicitly, for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ the maps $A_{\mathcal C}(U)\to A_{\mathcal C}(U)$ and $M(U)\to M(U)$ given by $s\mapsto as$ are injective. Neither a domain hypothesis on $A$ nor an enough-points hypothesis on $\mathcal C$ is required.

source.place: Tag 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact), applied to the constant ring presheaf A, followed by Tag 03ER (definition-flat), sheaf clause (3). The constant-module tensor-unit identification is in section-tensor-product.

proof.text: Write $R=A_{\mathcal C}$, let $O$ be the constant presheaf of commutative rings with value $A$, so that $\theta:O\to O^\#=R$ is its sheafification as a presheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and let $P$ be $O$ regarded as a presheaf of $O$-modules (its underlying presheaf of abelian groups is the constant presheaf with value the additive group of $A$). Multiplication $u:P\to P$, $x\mapsto ax$, has zero sectionwise kernel by the assumed injectivity on $A$. Abelian sheafification $\eta:P\to P^\#$ preserves finite limits, hence kernels and the zero object, by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]; therefore $u^\#:P^\#\to P^\#$ has zero kernel. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] the abelian sheaf $P^\#$ carries a unique $R$-module structure with $\theta(o)\eta(x)=\eta(ox)$, and $O$-linear maps from $P$ to $R$-modules extend uniquely to $R$-linear maps from $P^\#$. Identify $P^\#$ with $R$: the $O$-linear map $\theta:P\to R$ extends to an $R$-linear $\bar\theta:P^\#\to R$, and $\psi:R\to P^\#$, $r\mapsto r\,\eta(1)$, is $R$-linear. Then $\bar\theta\psi(r)=r\,\bar\theta(\eta(1))=r\theta(1)=r$; and $\psi\bar\theta$ is an $R$-linear endomorphism of $P^\#$ with $\psi\bar\theta\eta(o)=\theta(o)\eta(1)=\eta(o)$, so it is the identity by the uniqueness of extensions. Under $\bar\theta$, $u^\#$ is multiplication by the constant section $\theta(a)$: both $u^\#$ and $x\mapsto\theta(a)x$ are additive endomorphisms of $P^\#$ restricting along $\eta$ to $\eta(ox)\mapsto\eta(aox)=\theta(a)\eta(ox)$, and the extension along $\eta$ is unique [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Commutativity of $A$ makes this endomorphism $R$-linear. Its kernel, computed on underlying abelian sheaves, is zero, so it is monic in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$: cancellation holds on underlying abelian sheaves, hence on module morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03EI, lemma-sheafification-exact, via its underlying abelian sheafification proof; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, extended scalar action and universal property

proof.text: Construct the tensor-unit isomorphism $\lambda:R\otimes_R M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ using [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. On each object $U$, the balanced map $R(U)\otimes_{R(U)}M(U)\to M(U)$ is $r\otimes m\mapsto rm$, with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. The first composite is $m\mapsto m$; the second is $r\otimes m\mapsto1\otimes rm=r\otimes m$, by the balancing relation, and hence is the identity on all tensors. Both maps commute with restrictions because restrictions preserve $1$ and the module action. Thus the presheaf tensor is isomorphic to the underlying presheaf of the sheaf $M$; sheafifying gives the displayed isomorphism. In particular, this calculation does not assert that an arbitrary section of a sheaf tensor is globally a pure tensor.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, definition as sheafified sectionwise tensor; elementary tensor-unit calculation

proof.text: Let $T(N)=N\otimes_R M$. Flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] says exactly that $T$ is an exact functor on the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply the monomorphism-preservation clause (a) of [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] to the monomorphism $u^\#:R\to R$ from Step 1. It gives a monomorphism $v=u^\#\otimes1_M$ on $R\otimes_R M$. Under $\lambda$ from Step 2 this is multiplication by $a$: on the presheaf tensor $\lambda(v(r\otimes m))=\lambda(ar\otimes m)=(ar)m=a(rm)$. Equivalently, its conjugate sends $m$ to $\lambda(a\otimes m)=am$, by the explicit inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. These equalities hold after sheafification as equalities of the induced morphisms. Thus multiplication by $a$ on $M$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03ER, definition-flat (3), with Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; exact-functor tool: homology.tex Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor

proof.text: Kernels in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ are computed sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The two monomorphisms just proved therefore have zero kernels on every object $U$. If $as=at$ in either $R(U)$ or $M(U)$, then $s-t$ belongs to that zero kernel, so $s=t$. Conversely sectionwise injectivity implies cancellation of sheaf morphisms component by component. This proves the two explicit injectivity assertions and their stated monomorphism formulation. The argument used only injectivity of $x\mapsto ax$ on $A$ and exactness of sheaf tensor with $M$; it applies on any small site.
